interface.title: MiPrimer (Mi-Primer)
interface.field: Molecular biology: microRNA quantification by RT-qPCR
interface.stage_of_work: Assay design, before ordering oligos for miRNA qPCR
interface.what_it_is_for: Takes a mature miRNA sequence and builds candidate forward and reverse qPCR primers using the miR-specific qPCR rules of Balcells, Cirera & Busk 2011 (BMC Biotechnology 11:70), listing each primer's sequence, length, Tm and three pass/fail flags for A/T content at the 3' end. The reverse primers carry a poly-T stretch, so they are meant for poly(A)-tailed cDNA.

data.note: No data is loaded. The home page shows human let-7a-5p (UGAGGUAGUAGGUUGUAUAGUU) as an example, but it is plain text, not a clickable fill-in, so it has to be typed. I also typed miR-21-5p, miR-1-3p, miR-92a-3p and miR-16-5p from memory, plus a 16-nt prefix of miR-16.

tree.specific: Paste a mature miRNA sequence, get forward and reverse qPCR primers from the Balcells, Cirera & Busk 2011 rules, and pick ones with a suitable length and A/T content at the 3' end

children.note: Per the reviewer's reading of the code: a forward primer is a short 5' tail (from CGCAG) plus the 5' part of the miRNA; a reverse primer is a tail plus 15 T's plus the reverse complement of the miRNA's last 4–8 bases, so it only reads on poly(A)-tailed cDNA. The tool lists forward and reverse candidates separately and does not pair them.

children.general: Check that melting temperatures and lengths suit a standard cycling protocol
children.specific: Compare the Tm, °C and Length, bp columns. All candidates fell between about 59 and 61 °C; forward primers were 18–21 bp and reverse primers 24–30 bp
children.note: Every candidate reaches Tm > 59 °C because the tool lengthens the 5' tail until it does, so this check passes by design and does not separate candidates; length and the 3'-end flags are what differ.

features.name: Single-sequence design form with results tables
features.general: Paste one biological sequence, submit it, and get a results page with one table for each kind of candidate, showing the input sequence above them; press Back to edit the input and run it again
features.specific: Type a miRNA into 'MiRNA sequence', press Design or Enter, and read the Forward primers and Reverse primers tables (Sequence, Length bp, Tm °C, A–T on 3'). Browser Back keeps the last sequence in the field so it can be edited and resubmitted
steps: type or paste the RNA sequence (upper or lower case)
read the forward and reverse candidate tables under the echoed input
press browser Back, edit the sequence, and resubmit
serves_tasks: Submit a reference sequence and get candidate primers
Design primers for further targets and compare the yield
Edit the previous input and run it again
Check whether the input is case-sensitive
Check that melting temperatures and lengths suit a standard cycling protocol

features.name: 3'-end quality traffic-light flags with hover explanations
features.general: Show each candidate's pass/fail on several sequence-end rules as a row of small green or red squares; hover a square to read which rule it is and why it passed or failed
features.specific: In the 'A–T on 3'' column, three squares check (in order) whether the last 5 bases contain 2–3 A/T, the last 3 bases contain 1–2 A/T, and the last 2 bases contain 1 A/T. Green means pass, red means fail; hovering shows a tooltip such as 'Last 3 bases at the 3`end don`t include 1-2 A or T residues'. The tooltip sometimes needs a second hover to appear
steps: scan the squares for red ones
hover a square to see which window (last 5, 3 or 2 bases) it checks
read whether that rule passed or failed
prefer candidates with all green squares, then compare length
serves_tasks: Find candidates whose 3' end is likely to misprime

features.name: Input validation with error messages
features.general: Reject input that is out of the allowed length range or uses the wrong alphabet, and say which rule was broken
features.specific: Only 16–39 nt inputs are accepted; anything shorter or longer (including empty, and exactly 15 or 40 nt per the code) gives 'MiRNA string length should be lay between 15 and 40 nucleotides', a message that misstates the range. Non-RNA letters give 'Not an RNA string'. Both appear as raw Werkzeug debugger traceback pages, not as messages inside the form
steps: submit an empty, too short or too long sequence and read the length message
submit a DNA (T-containing) sequence and read the alphabet message
go back to the form and correct the input
serves_tasks: Submit input that breaks a validation rule and read the error
Submit a sequence that is too short
Submit a sequence that is too long
Submit a sequence with the wrong alphabet

screens_never_reached: A results page reached by URL: GET /primers?mirna=... returns 405 Method Not Allowed (screens/031.webp). Results only come from submitting the form, so they cannot be bookmarked or shared as a link
A friendly error message inside the form: invalid input only produces debugger traceback pages
not_done: Filling the field from the example: clicking the let-7a example text under the field did nothing; it is plain text, not a link (screens/002.webp)
Sorting or filtering candidates: the table headers are not interactive (clicking 'Tm, °C' did nothing, screens/030.webp)
Exporting or downloading primers: there is no export, copy button or download. Sequences can only be selected by hand (screens/029.webp)

Getting forward primers for miR-21, miR-1 and miR-92a: the tool returned an empty Forward primers table for each with no on-page explanation. The reviewer's reading of the code says this is the intended result of the prefix-length, 3'-end and Tm rules (see t6), but the interface itself never says so

Testing the exact length limits: I tried 10, 16, 22 and 45 nt, not 15 or 40 nt. The error text says 15–40 nt, while the code (len > 15 and < 40) and repository accept 16–39; the 15- and 40-nt cases were not tried in the interface
Exploring the Werkzeug traceback frames and debugger console: they belong to the server's developer tools, not to the scientific workflow
Tooltip on the miR-21 red square (screens/008.webp): I hovered it but did not capture the tooltip, because the screenshot came before the tooltip's delay ran out
